PlanTicketDraft.description:
One ticket in a proposed set, before anything is filed.

It has no id. Ids belong to the backlog and only the filer can see the backlog, so a draft is
identified by its slug — which is also what its filename becomes. Dependencies inside a plan are
therefore slugs too: ``ARCA-075`` does not exist yet and writing it into a draft would be writing
down a guess.

body.description:
The full ticket markdown, in the house format. Filed verbatim apart from two lines the
filer owns: the id in the heading, and the ``Depends on`` line, which cannot be written
until the ids exist.
body.title: Body

depends_on.description:
Slugs of other tickets in THIS plan that must land first. Slugs, never ids: nothing in
a draft has an id. Must be acyclic and must name tickets present in the same plan.
depends_on.title: Depends On

source.description:
Where in the founder's document this came from — a section heading, a page, a quoted
line. A founder must be able to check that the machine did not invent a requirement, and
that check is impossible if the ticket cannot say where it came from.
source.title: Source

struck.description:
The founder struck this line. A struck ticket is not filed, and every dependency on it
is spliced out of the rest of the set rather than left pointing at nothing.
struck.title: Struck

A lowercase-kebab name, the same shape the ticket filer already accepts. Bounded and

description:
A set of tickets proposed from one document, before a founder has agreed to any of it
(fountainbridge FB-127, gap G5).

A founder arrives with a PRD, a deck, a page of notes, and watches it become N draft tickets in
dependency order — smallest shippable first, each line struck or kept, filed as one set on one
press. Today they would file one ticket, then another, describing the same document from memory
each time.

**Nothing here is filed.** A plan draft is inert: it opens no branch, writes no file and reserves
no id. It becomes work only when a founder presses once, and that press is the only thing in the
system that turns a plan into tickets. That is why the shape carries no ids — an id is evidence a
backlog was written to, and a draft has written to nothing.

Filed as ONE branch, ONE pull request and N ticket files. The set is one decision and lands as one,
which is also what lets the ids allocate correctly in a single pass (FB-117) and at the backlog's
own width (FB-118).

The venture repository the set would be filed into. Named in the draft rather than
chosen at filing time, so the tickets a founder read are the tickets that land, in the
